verifier_note: All factual checks executed against the read-only snapshot; scratch in /tmp/t01 (smoke.py reproduces the artifact's own step-4 self-test and its failure mode). Theme T07's verdicts are treated as established input and are cited, not re-derived: T07-X1 (Div. column is a literal 0 at paper/scripts/gen_tables.py:184; root column regex-scraped from testbench source; no observed root retained; PASS == observed==EXPECTED(N); zero SIM_FAIL_BYPASS rows), T07-D144 (the observable is the ALU latch, not DMEM), T07 positive control (16/16 canonical roots reproduce exactly).

verdicts.finding: Eight of the sixteen rows of the invariance table have a single (G, topology) point and therefore carry no cross-reshape evidence at all.
verdicts.observed: Recounted from snapshot/benchmarks/instances.csv joined to results/results/live_hw_results_p1_unified.csv (script /tmp/t01, python csv): per-N distinct (G,topology) points are 8->2, 10->1, 16->1, 32->3, 50->1, 100->1, 128->6, 200->1, 500->1, 512->6, 1024->5, 1500->1, 2048->4, 3000->1, 4096->3, 8192->2 HW-validated (3 compiled). Exactly eight rows -- N=10,16,50,100,200,500,1500,3000 -- have one point. Their passing configuration counts are 17+21+25+33+44+98+104+77 = 419 of 2,822 (14.9%). The passing-count column I recomputed reproduces paper/tables/invariance.tex column 4 for all sixteen rows exactly (28,17,21,102,25,33,371,44,98,456,425,104,437,77,331,253; sum 2,822). r03's and r07's numbers are exact.
verdicts.what_is_true: The count is exact. But the consequence 'no cross-reshape evidence at all' is too strong for seven of the eight rows once one looks at what the compiler actually did with the fabric it was given. Recomputing the number of PEs the assignment actually populates (sw_results.csv column n_gpus_used) over passing configurations: N=10 spans 3-4 workers, N=16 4-5, N=50 6-7, N=100 9-10, N=500 30-32, N=1500 50-64, N=3000 121-128. Only N=200 (npow2_med_fat) is a true singleton: all 44 passing configurations place nodes on exactly 12 PEs. Counting distinct (workers-actually-used, topology) pairs instead of (provisioned G, topology), 15 of 16 rows have >=2 points and the totals become N=128->12, N=512->14, N=1024->12, N=2048->11, N=4096->9. Separately, all 2,822 passing configurations are distinct program images (tb_hash is unique within each instance; npass == #distinct tb_hash on every instance), so every row does witness complete replacement of the assignment and mapping algorithms even where G and topology are fixed.
verdicts.consequence: CLARIFY LIMITATION, one clause, and take the credit that is already earned. The honest sentence is: 'eight of the sixteen leaf counts are represented by a single provisioned (G, topology) point; at those N the invariance is witnessed across assignment, mapping and schedule but not across reshape, and 2,403 of the 2,822 configurations (85.1%) lie at N with two or more (G, topology) points.' Adding a second instance at each singleton N is NOT required -- the claim narrowing costs zero pages and the eight small instances would add ~8 x 20 = 160 xsim runs for a cosmetic gain.

verdicts.finding: Reproducibility checklist points at the wrong table column and mis-describes the root values as SHA-256 hashes.
verdicts.observed: paper/main.tex:3099-3101 reads 'Every HW-validated configuration at the same $N$ produces a 64-bit root whose SHA-256 matches the column 4 of Table~\ref{tab:invariance}.' paper/tables/invariance.tex header line 8-9 gives the column order as 1 $N$, 2 compiled (G,topo), 3 HW-val. (G,topo), 4 'HW configs (passing)', 5 '64-bit root result'. Column 4 entries are counts (28, 17, 21, 102, ...); column 5 entries are raw 16-hex-digit big-endian FP64 words (\texttt{0x40E1948E978D4FDF}), not SHA-256 digests. Both r06 and r14 are exactly right.
verdicts.what_is_true: Two errors in one sentence: wrong column index and wrong hash type. A third follows from T07-X1: no per-run root or hash of a per-run root exists anywhere in the artifact, so even the corrected sentence would describe a check a reader cannot perform on the released data.
verdicts.consequence: EDIT. Replace with: 'Canonical root per $N$. Column 5 of Table~\ref{tab:invariance} is the 64-bit canonical root $\Rcan(N,L)$ as a big-endian hex word; it is reproduced by tools/... from Definitions 1-3 and eq.(20) and is the constant every passing testbench compares against.' Zero page cost; leaving it is a free hit for any referee who opens the table.

verdicts.finding: Confirmation: all sixteen canonical root values reproduce bit-exactly from the paper's own definitions, and the descriptive statistics reconcile.
verdicts.observed: Not re-derived here -- already independently reconfirmed twice in theme T07 (T07 positive-control section: reimplementation of make_leaf_val (sprs_core.py:5364-5370) plus the heap-indexed CBTree gives 16/16 exact matches to paper/tables/invariance.tex, cross-checked through the project's own _fp64_add_bits). I independently reconfirmed the *table-count* half of the claim from the released CSV: the compiled / HW-val / passing columns of all sixteen rows and the 2,822 total regenerate exactly from results/results/live_hw_results_p1_unified.csv joined to benchmarks/instances.csv. I also reproduced the paper's 278 IMEM rejections exactly (large_extreme_1d 120, vlarge_extreme_1d 120, max_bal_2d 10, max_mod_fat 10, maxp_bal_2d 10, maxp_mod_fat 8) and \WallTotalH=821.5 core-hours over passing rows (recomputed 821.5 from live_hw_results_p1_maxpe.csv).
verdicts.what_is_true: The arithmetic of the paper is sound: the oracle constants are right and every count in the invariance table reconciles to the released data. What the reproduction does NOT establish is that the fabric produced those constants -- that is T07-X1, and it is answered there (PASS is by construction observed==EXPECTED(N), 2,822 times, with zero SIM_FAIL_BYPASS rows).
verdicts.consequence: NO CHANGE. This is corroborating evidence, not an issue. Cite it in the rebuttal letter rather than the paper.

verdicts.finding: The 64-bit root column is scraped from the compiler's own EXPECTED constant; the divergence column is a hard-coded literal zero and no per-run root is retained.
verdicts.observed: Established and settled as T07-X1; I re-verified the three load-bearing lines rather than re-deriving the theme. paper/scripts/gen_tables.py:105-120 canonical_roots() regex-scrapes rb"EXPECTED\s*=\s*64'h([0-9A-Fa-f]{16})" out of the emitted tb_*.sv files; :157 'assert len(exps) == 1'; :183-185 emits the row as f"{N:<5} & {nc} & {nv} & {ncfg} & \\texttt{{0x{root}}} & 0 & " -- the Div. cell is the literal character '0' in the format string. Released CSV headers: live_hw_results_p1_maxpe.csv = Instance,Pipeline,TB_Name,Pass,Cycles,SimTime_s,ErrorCode,Error,CyclesGPU0,PerfAllGPUs; live_hw_results_p1_unified.csv is headerless with the same first eight fields. Neither has a root column; grep 'root_result' over both returns 0 hits. experiments/phase1/_bypass_runner.py:128-139 parses only [PASS]/TIMEOUT/[FAIL] and the perf vector, and :163 shutil.rmtree(wd) destroys the xsim log. No tb_*.sv is in the snapshot either (find . -name 'tb_*' -> 0 files), so even the scrape is not reproducible from the artifact.
verdicts.what_is_true: Every element of the finding is literally true. The consequence the reviewer draws -- 'what is unverifiable is that the fabric produced them, which is precisely the claim' -- is where T07-X1 already ruled: PASS in the testbench (sprs_core.py:5573) is exactly (all_done && root PE result == EXPECTED), EXPECTED provably depends on N alone, and there are zero SIM_FAIL_BYPASS rows in any released CSV. So the measurement is real; the *presentation* passes off a literal and a compiler constant as measured columns.
verdicts.consequence: REWRITE the two columns, do not re-run. Relabel 'Div.' as 'Root mismatches' and state in the caption that it is computed as the count of rows with ErrorCode==SIM_FAIL_BYPASS (0 of 2,844) and that all non-passing runs are timeouts; relabel '64-bit root result' as 'canonical root $\Rcan(N,L)$ (compared against by every testbench)'. Add the observed-root column to the collector for any future run. Re-running 2,822 configurations to record a value already known to equal the constant is the most expensive answer available and buys nothing a referee can use.

verdicts.finding: 32 RTL runs did not reach a verdict and are reported nowhere; the zero-divergence denominator is silently restricted to terminating runs.
verdicts.observed: live_hw_results_p1_maxpe.csv: 2,854 data rows, Pass=Counter({True:2822, False:32}), ErrorCode=Counter({OK_BYPASS:2822, SIM_TB_TIMEOUT_BYPASS:21, SIM_WALLCLOCK_TIMEOUT_BYPASS:11}) -- r04 reproduces exactly. BUT the 2,854 rows cover only 2,844 distinct (Instance, TB_Name) keys: max_mod_fat/tb_2f_3a_none appears 10 times and maxp_bal_2d/tb_2f_3a_none twice. So the 32 non-passing ROWS are 22 non-passing CONFIGURATIONS plus 10 retries. live_hw_results_p1_unified.csv -- which is the file gen_tables.py:29 actually reads -- has exactly 2,844 rows, 2,844 distinct keys, 2,822 pass / 22 fail (21 SIM_TB_TIMEOUT + 1 SIM_WALLCLOCK). Core-hours recomputed from SimTime_s: passing 821.5 (= \WallTotalH exactly), non-passing 122.9, maxp_mod_fat 58.9. r04's '~123 core-hours' is exact. Confirmed that neither 2,844 nor 2,854 nor any of the 22/32 appears in paper/main.tex (grep for 844, 854, 920 finds only an unrelated hash substring) and neither appears in companion/main.tex.
verdicts.what_is_true: The correct denominator is 2,844 attempted unique configurations, 2,822 passing, 22 non-settling -- not 32. 32 is a row count inflated by 10 retries of two configurations. 122.9 core-hours (12.3% of the campaign's true 1,003.3 core-h) are spent on runs the paper never mentions. r04's second point is the important one and is correct: these are the paper's only observed instance of Property 2 outcome (c), and they are thrown away.
verdicts.consequence: ADD ANALYSIS + CLARIFY, ~0.15 page, and it is a net gain not a concession. Report '2,844 attempted, 2,822 passing, 22 non-settling' once in Sec 7.1 and add three sentences classifying the 22 (see T01-X5, which classifies them from data already in hand). Also correct \WallTotalH's framing: 821.5 core-h is over passing runs only; the campaign cost 1,003.3 core-h.

verdicts.finding: The measured 64-bit root is never recorded per run in the released data; the central table column and the reproducibility-checklist item cannot be checked from the artifact.
verdicts.observed: Same evidence as D018. Column lists verified directly from the two CSV headers; 'root_result' appears 0 times in either. r04's mitigating half is also confirmed (independently, in T07): the software oracle reproduces all sixteen roots exactly, and the heap-vs-visual leaf-order difference shows up at N=200 only, 1 ulp.
verdicts.what_is_true: Identical in substance to D018/D053. Three reviewers on three different views found the same fact; it is not in dispute.
verdicts.consequence: Merge with D018. One fix serves all three: relabel the two columns, state the timeouts-not-mismatches fact, and add the root column to the collector for future runs. Do not re-simulate.

verdicts.finding: 98 unique testbenches produced no verdict and are excluded from the zero-divergence denominator; only 5 are disclosed, and the non-settling runs cluster on specific algorithms.
verdicts.observed: Recomputed over all 40 results/results/*/sw_results.csv: 7,200 software rows (exactly 180 per instance on all 40), 2,920 with unique_hw_sim==True, of which maxp_mod_fat contributes 76 and the other 39 instances 2,844. live_hw_results_maxp_mod_fat.csv has 5 rows, all SIM_WALLCLOCK_TIMEOUT_BYPASS, so 71 of maxp_mod_fat's 76 were never attempted. 22 of the 2,844 never settled. 22 + 76 = 98 of 2,920 = 3.36%. r05's ledger is exact. Clustering confirmed from the maxpe CSV: vlarge2_mod_ring 2i|3{a,b,c,d,e,f,h,i,j} (9 CPOP runs, stopping at 44,969-44,975) plus 2f|3a; vlarge_dense_hc 2g|3{a,b,c,f,g,i,j} (7 DSC runs, all at exactly 20,897); 2f|3a (DFSseed) on max_bal_2d, max_dense_hc, maxp_dense_hc, maxp_bal_2d, max_mod_fat, vlarge2_mod_ring.
verdicts.what_is_true: The 98/2,920 ledger is right. ONE SUB-NUMBER IS WRONG: r05 says 'Sixteen of the 32 report a positive cycle count with Pass=False'. Recounted: 21 of the 32 rows have Cycles>0 and 11 have Cycles=-1 (the wall-clock kills). The right figure is 21. Also, 'never attempted' and 'did not settle' are different in kind and should not be pooled into one 98: 71 maxp_mod_fat images were never given to the simulator at all (a resource decision, already disclosed in spirit by L0), 5 were attempted and hit the 28,800 s wall-clock, and 22 on validated instances ran and did not settle.
verdicts.consequence: CLARIFY LIMITATION with a four-line ledger, not a table: attempted 2,844 + 5, passing 2,822, fabric fail-stop 21, wall-clock timeout 6, never attempted 71. That is the whole disclosure and it costs about a fifth of a page. Do not build the per-instance table r05 asks for -- put that in the companion.

verdicts.finding: Headline invariance evidence (the 64-bit root values themselves) is not present in the released results; only PASS/FAIL verdicts are.
verdicts.observed: Same as D018/D046. r06's own positive checks also reproduce: all 2,822 passing rows carry OK_BYPASS; all non-passing rows are SIM_TB_TIMEOUT_BYPASS or SIM_WALLCLOCK_TIMEOUT_BYPASS; SIM_FAIL_BYPASS occurs 0 times in maxpe, unified and the maxp_mod_fat CSV; no Error field contains 'root_result' or '[ERROR]'.
verdicts.what_is_true: Duplicate of D018 in substance, from an independent view. Its useful contribution is the negative check: no divergence hides in the failures.
verdicts.consequence: Merge with D018. Report the negative check in the paper -- it is free and it is the strongest sentence available about the failures.

verdicts.finding: 21 compiled configurations failed hardware validation with fabric-raised timeouts, all on cyclic topologies, and the paper does not mention them.
verdicts.observed: Confirmed exactly. The 21 SIM_TB_TIMEOUT_BYPASS rows are vlarge2_mod_ring x10 (ring), vlarge_dense_hc x7 (hypercube_5d), max_dense_hc, maxp_dense_hc (hypercube), max_bal_2d, maxp_bal_2d (torus): zero on linear, mesh or fat-tree. rtl/btree_pkg.sv:22-23 gives TIMEOUT_MAX=10000, WATCHDOG_MAX=20000. The largest passing run in the campaign is 19,250 cycles on vlarge2_bal_fat 2f|3a -- r09's number is exact. TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) r09 attributes the 20,897 cluster on vlarge_dense_hc to TIMEOUT_MAX=10,000 'continuous EX stall'. It is the watchdog: rtl/btree_fsm_fast.sv:779-787 resets watchdog on any retire, so a PE that last retired at cycle 897 errors at 20,897 = 897 + 20,000. Every one of the 21 fits X + 20,000 for small X: 20,023 = 23+20k, 20,038, 20,068, 20,075, 20,897 = 897+20k, 44,969 = 24,969+20k. All 21 are WATCHDOG_MAX fires. (2) The 'headroom' inference is a category error: watchdog counts CONSECUTIVE non-retiring cycles, not total cycles (btree_fsm_fast.sv:783 'watchdog <= any_retired ? 0 : watchdog + 1'), so a 19,250-cycle passing run is not at 96% of any ceiling. The real ceiling a long schedule must respect is 20,000 consecutive stalled cycles on one PE, which no passing run came near.
verdicts.what_is_true: 21 fabric watchdog fail-stops, all on ring/torus/hypercube, none disclosed. The topology correlation is real. The '96% of the liveness ceiling' scalability worry is not: it compares a total-cycle count to a consecutive-stall threshold.
verdicts.consequence: ADD ANALYSIS from data in hand (T01-X5) and REFUSE the scalability framing. Do not re-run with transcript capture: the classification is already derivable. Reporting '21 configurations, all on cyclic topologies, fail-stopped in the fabric's watchdog' is a positive result for Property 2, and the topology concentration is an honest, interesting observation that costs one sentence.

verdicts.finding: 32 RTL runs did not settle -- 21 fabric watchdog fail-stops -- and are excluded from the reported distribution without disclosure; all 32 have connected==False, which links this to the omitted S2.5 pass.
verdicts.observed: Census confirmed (see D039: 32 rows = 22 configurations). Per-instance non-passing rows in maxpe: vlarge2_mod_ring 10, vlarge_dense_hc 7, max_mod_fat 10, maxp_bal_2d 2, max_bal_2d 1, max_dense_hc 1, maxp_dense_hc 1 -- r11 exact. 'not one SIM_FAIL_BYPASS row anywhere' -- confirmed, 0 in all three CSVs. THE CONNECTIVITY INFERENCE IS THE OVER-REACH. Joining the unified CSV to sw_results.csv on (instance, tb_fname): (Pass, connected) = {(True,False):2061, (True,True):761, (False,False):22}. So yes, all 22 non-settling configurations are disconnected -- but so are 2,061 of the 2,822 that passed. P(fail | disconnected) = 22/2083 = 1.06%; P(fail | connected) = 0/761. Fisher exact two-sided p = 0.0013, so the association is statistically real, but disconnection is 99% benign and cannot be the explanation.
verdicts.what_is_true: The census and the 'no wrong root anywhere' fact are exact. The claim that connected==False 'links this directly to the omitted S2.5 pass' is not supported: disconnection is the normal case in this campaign (73% of passing runs) and predicts failure at about one in a hundred.
verdicts.consequence: Report the census; do NOT adopt the S2.5 causal story in the paper. If S2.5 is discussed elsewhere, the correct statement is 'all 22 non-settling configurations had disconnected PE partitions, as did 2,061 of the 2,822 that passed' -- which is honest and simultaneously defuses the reviewer's inference. Zero page cost, and it pre-empts the same objection at the next round.

verdicts.finding: The artifact's own headline self-test for bitwise invariance cannot fail.
verdicts.observed: Verified by execution, not by reading. tools/smoke_test.sh:57-77 step 4 builds a testbench for (G,topo) in {(4,hypercube),(8,fat_tree),(16,torus),(2,linear)} at N=32, regex-extracts EXPECTED from the emitted string, and asserts len(set(roots))==1. I ran that code (/tmp/t01/smoke.py, importing snapshot/src/sprs_core.py read-only): all four give 0x41201D1FCED91687 (which is also Table V's N=32 row). I then re-ran it with the assignment AND mapping deliberately scrambled (every node moved to PE (p+1) mod G, i.e. a gross C-bind/C-conn violation): all four still give 0x41201D1FCED91687, and the emitted testbench length changes (33478 -> 33484 bytes on the torus), proving the image really did change while EXPECTED did not. Sweeping 18 (S2,S3) combinations gives one distinct EXPECTED (plus AlgoBypassed for 2e).
verdicts.what_is_true: The self-test labelled 'The ABI holds: same N, different G and topology, same root' compares the compiler's own prediction against itself. It is invariant under arbitrary corruption of the very thing it purports to test, so its assertion cannot fire. This is the same tautology as gen_tables.py:157 (T07-X1), shipped to the reader as the artifact's headline check.
verdicts.consequence: CHANGE IMPLEMENTATION, cheap and high-value for artifact evaluation. Either (a) make step 4 hash the emitted IMEM's COMPUTE operand-address bindings under the canonical node order and assert THAT is invariant -- a genuine test of C-bind that runs in seconds with no simulator -- or (b) relabel it honestly as 'the compiler predicts the same root at every (G,topology)' and move the real check into step 5. Option (a) is ~15 lines and turns the artifact's weakest exhibit into its most convincing. This is the one CHANGE IMPLEMENTATION in T01 I would actually spend on, because artifact reviewers run smoke_test.sh first.

verdicts.finding: The 22 non-passing hardware runs are never reported; the denominator 2,844 does not appear in the paper; the per-run logs needed to check them against Property 2 are not retained.
verdicts.observed: live_hw_results_p1_unified.csv: 2,844 data rows, {OK_BYPASS:2822, SIM_TB_TIMEOUT_BYPASS:21, SIM_WALLCLOCK_TIMEOUT_BYPASS:1} -- r12 exact. grep over paper/main.tex confirms 2,844 never appears; the only '844' hit is inside an unrelated hash at :3097. Log retention confirmed: experiments/phase1/_bypass_runner.py:133-134 keeps only lines containing 'TIMEOUT' on the timeout branch, and :163 shutil.rmtree(wd) deletes the xsim log. I checked every Error field in all three CSVs: '[ERROR]' 0 hits, 'State=' 0 hits. logs/ contains only phase1_rerun.log and phase1_sw.log; no xsim transcript.
verdicts.what_is_true: Exact. r12's conclusion -- 'whether the fabric raised P_ERROR cannot be determined from the artifact' -- is the only part that is too pessimistic, and T01-X5 shows why: the retained per-PE perf_total vector settles it without the transcript.
verdicts.consequence: CLARIFY + ADD ANALYSIS. State the denominator once, list the 22 by instance in the companion, and give the fail-stop classification in the paper. The 're-run them with full transcript capture' that r12 asks for is unnecessary and would cost ~120 core-hours to learn what the perf vector already says.

verdicts.finding: Verified: the canonical tree, leaf enumeration, leaf formula and all sixteen reported root values reproduce exactly.
verdicts.observed: Independently reconfirmed in theme T07 (positive-control section), three ways, 16/16 exact, including the N=7 visual-order example and the N=200 one-ulp heap-vs-visual difference. Not re-derived here.
verdicts.what_is_true: The oracle side of the result is solid and has now been reproduced by four independent implementations (r05, r09, r14, and the T07 verifier).
verdicts.consequence: NO CHANGE. Use it in the response letter: four reviewers independently reproduced the sixteen roots.

verdicts.finding: Claim 1 universally quantifies over 'all valid ... refinements $r$', but zero of the 2,822 RTL-validated configurations -- indeed zero of the 7,200 compiled configurations -- apply any refinement.
verdicts.observed: Claim 1 verbatim, paper/main.tex:813-828: '... for all $(G,\mathrm{topology}) \in \T$, all valid assignments $\asgn$, mappings $\map$, refinements $r$, and schedules $s$ emitted by \sv{build\_schedule}, the observed 64-bit root DMEM value at program termination equals $\Rcan(N,L)$.' Every TB_Name in live_hw_results_p1_unified.csv ends in '_none': the S4 field of all 2,822 passing rows is 'none' (Counter has exactly one key). Across all forty sw_results.csv files, the s4 column is empty in 7,200 of 7,200 rows, and in 2,920 of 2,920 unique_hw_sim rows. sprs_core.STAGE4_METHODS has 12 entries with '4a' = 'None' (refine_none); sprs_tournament.enumerate_s4_configs() yields 122. So the campaign covers 1 of 122 refinement configurations, and that one is the identity. main.tex:2066 nevertheless describes 'Phase 2: Top-15 unique Phase-1 winners crossed with 122 S4 refinements; same selection and validation' as part of the protocol, and no released artifact contains a Phase-2 result. (The mutation campaign is the sole place refined images appear: results/mutation/mutation_results.json references tb_2a_3a_4g and tb_2a_3a_4c2 on 7 of its 20 instances -- but those are mutants, not invariance evidence.)
verdicts.what_is_true: The refinement axis of Claim 1's quantifier has exactly zero RTL evidence and exactly zero software evidence in the released data. The paper's own honest sentence at main.tex:1900-1902 ('The remainder of the ~22,000-point space is covered by the argument above rather than by measurement') is true but understates the asymmetry: it is not that a fraction of the space is unmeasured, it is that one of the three algorithmic dimensions is wholly unmeasured. Relatedly, main.tex:2168-2172 says 'each configuration is additionally the product of a different compiler triple $(\asgn, \map, r)$' -- $r$ is identical across all 2,822.
verdicts.consequence: REMOVE OR NARROW CLAIM, zero page cost, and it is the single most exposed sentence in the paper for a referee who opens the CSV. Three edits: (1) in Claim 1 either drop 'refinements $r$' from the quantifier or add 'refinements $r$ (evaluated at $r = $ identity in this campaign)'; (2) at main.tex:2170 change '$(\asgn, \map, r)$' to '$(\asgn, \map)$'; (3) delete or re-tense the Phase 2 bullet at main.tex:2066 -- describing a phase that produced no released data invites exactly the question the authors do not want asked. If the argument for refinement-invariance is structural (S4 permutes placement only), say so in one clause: that is a perfectly respectable answer and costs nothing.

verdicts.finding: UNDERSTATEMENT: the paper describes a top-15-per-instance selection into RTL validation, but the released campaign simulated every deduplicated testbench of the complete 18x10 grid -- so the invariance evidence is subject to no makespan-based selection at all.
verdicts.observed: main.tex:2063-2065: 'Phase 1. 180 baseline $(S2,S3)$ configurations evaluated by the software cost model. Top-15 per instance by \sv{makespan} promoted to Phase~3 xsim validation, with testbench-hash deduplication.' That is not what ran. src/sprs_tournament.py:1204-1240 (and the hw_only path at :2010-2038) queues for xsim EVERY first occurrence of each distinct tb_hash per instance -- 'if key not in leader_map: res["unique_hw_sim"] = True ... vivado_queue.append(...)' -- and select_winners(..., max_per=15) is only called AFTERWARDS (:2245, :2255), for reporting and Phase-2 promotion. The data agree: per-instance passing counts over the 39 HW-validated instances range from 12 to 141 with median 74, and 38 of the 39 exceed 15 -- and the paper's own Table X (paper/tables/walltime.tex) prints those same numbers in its 'TBs' column (e.g. \sv{maxp_bal_2d} 141, \sv{max_bal_2d} 131, \sv{vlarge_bal_mesh} 127). A referee who reads Sec 7.1 and then Table X sees 15 promised and up to 141 delivered.
verdicts.what_is_true: The RTL campaign is the full 18x10 S2xS3 grid on every one of the 40 instances (7,200 = 40 x 180 compilations, exactly 180 rows in every sw_results.csv), reduced by SHA-256 testbench-hash dedup to 2,920 distinct program images, of which 2,844 were attempted and 2,822 settled. No makespan ranking gates any of it. The paper describes a weaker protocol than it executed, and it contradicts its own Table X.
verdicts.consequence: EDIT, negative page cost, large positive acceptance effect. Rewrite the Phase-1 bullet to what happened: 'the complete $18\times10$ $(S2,S3)$ grid is compiled on every instance (7,200 compilations); testbench-hash deduplication leaves 2,920 distinct program images, and every one on a hardware-validated instance is simulated. Ranking by \sv{makespan} is used only to select performance winners, and plays no part in the invariance evidence.' This simultaneously fixes the self-contradiction, removes any selection-bias worry from the headline result, and lets the top-15 language stay where it belongs (the performance sections). It is the largest free win in this theme.

verdicts.finding: 116 of the 2,844 RTL-validated configurations are ones the compiler itself rejected for IMEM overflow; 113 of them sit inside the headline 2,822.
verdicts.observed: Over the 2,920 unique_hw_sim rows the error_code histogram is {E_OK: 2803, E_IMEM_OF: 117}. 116 of the 117 are on HW-validated instances (large_extreme_1d 46, vlarge_extreme_1d 67, max_bal_2d 1, max_mod_fat 1, maxp_bal_2d 1; the 117th is maxp_mod_fat's, never attempted). All 116 appear in live_hw_results_p1_unified.csv: 113 Pass=True, 3 timeouts. Their recorded max_imem ranges 518 to 1792 against the 512-entry budget. The mechanism is src/sprs_core.py:5380-5383 in emit_sv_testbench: 'max_imem = max(len(progs[g]) ...); imem_sz = 1; while imem_sz < max_imem: imem_sz *= 2; imem_sz = max(imem_sz, 64)' -- the emitted testbench sizes IMEM to the next power of two above the longest program, overriding rtl/btree_pkg.sv:19 'parameter int IMEM_DEPTH = 512'. Paper main.tex:2019-2023 states 'IMEM and DMEM are fixed at 512 entries per PE ... which the S5 memory pass checks and rejects rather than truncating. This is not a hypothetical: 278 of the 7,200 compilations were rejected this way.' I reproduce 278 exactly (120/120/10/10/10/8), and the paper's per-instance attributions for large_extreme_1d, vlarge_extreme_1d, max_mod_fat and maxp_mod_fat are all correct; it omits max_bal_2d 10 and maxp_bal_2d 10.
verdicts.what_is_true: 'Rejected' and 'counted in the headline' are both true of 113 configurations. This cuts both ways and the favourable side is larger: the invariance evidence extends to PEs with 1024- and 2048-entry IMEMs, i.e. beyond the resource model priced in Table IV, which is a genuine robustness datum. The unfavourable side is a flat contradiction between 'rejects rather than truncating' and the presence of those images in the validated set, plus the fact that the simulated fabric is not always the 512-entry fabric the paper costs out.
verdicts.consequence: CLARIFY, one sentence, and take the credit. 'The emitted testbench sizes IMEM to the next power of two above the longest per-PE program, so 116 configurations that the S5 pass flags as exceeding the 512-entry budget were nevertheless simulated (with 1024- or 2048-entry IMEM) and are included in Table V; 113 of them pass. The S5 rejection is a deployment gate on the fixed-size fabric, not a compile failure.' Leaving it unstated is the risk: an artifact reviewer who joins sw_results.csv to the HW CSV finds a 116-row contradiction in five minutes.

verdicts.finding: The abstract's coverage arithmetic mixes per-instance and campaign-total counts, inflating apparent search-space coverage by a factor of 40.
verdicts.observed: Abstract and main.tex:150-152: 'a seven-stage compiler whose algorithmic configuration space spans $18\times 10\times 122 \approx 22{,}000$ assignment/mapping/refinement combinations, of which this campaign compiles $7{,}200$ and validates $2{,}822$ in RTL.' 18 x 10 x 122 = 21,960, which is a PER-INSTANCE count. 7,200 is 40 instances x 180 (S2,S3) pairs -- verified: every one of the forty sw_results.csv files has exactly 180 rows, and the 180 distinct (s2,s3) pairs are the full 18 x 10 grid. Per instance the campaign compiles 180 of 21,960 = 0.82%; the reader computing 7,200/22,000 gets 32.8%.
verdicts.what_is_true: The two numbers are not commensurable. The defensible statements are: the campaign compiles the complete $18\times10$ $(S2,S3)$ grid on every one of the 40 instances, and covers 1 of the 122 S4 refinement configurations.
verdicts.consequence: EDIT, zero page cost, and the honest version is rhetorically stronger. 'The campaign compiles the complete $18\times10$ assignment-by-mapping grid on all 40 instances (7,200 compilations) at the identity refinement, and validates 2,822 of the resulting distinct program images in RTL.' Exhaustive-over-two-axes beats 33%-of-a-space that turns out to be 0.8%.

verdicts.finding: The 21 undisclosed non-settling runs can be classified as fabric watchdog fail-stops from data already in the released CSV, with no re-simulation -- turning the theme's largest liability into the paper's only direct evidence for Property 2 outcome (c).
verdicts.observed: Four facts compose. (1) rtl/btree_fsm_fast.sv:885-902: 'cnt_total' increments only while pstate is P_RUN or P_DRAIN, so a PE's perf_total freezes the cycle it enters P_ERROR or P_DONE. (2) The testbench's own loop cap is timeout_cycles = max(200000, total_nodes*1000)/10 (src/sprs_core.py:5494, 5562) = 204,700 cycles for N=1024, 409,500 for N=2048, 819,100 for N=4096, 1,638,300 for N=8192. (3) The retained PerfAllGPUs vector in live_hw_results_p1_maxpe.csv gives every PE's final counter for 21 of the 22 non-settling configurations. I tabulated them: max-over-PE is 20,023 / 20,038 / 20,068 / 20,075 / 20,897 / 44,969-44,975 -- between 5x and 82x BELOW the loop cap -- and the maximum is attained by 1 to 48 PEs out of 32 to 2,070, with minima as low as 5. Since a PE still in P_RUN would have counted all the way to the cap, no PE was still running when the simulation ended. (4) rtl/noc_system.sv:300 'assign all_done = &cn_done', and the testbench printed TIMEOUT, so all_done was low, so at least one PE was not in P_DONE. A PE that is neither running nor done is in P_ERROR. Therefore all 21 are fabric fail-stops. The specific guard is identifiable too: btree_fsm_fast.sv:779-787 resets the watchdog on any retire, so a WATCHDOG_MAX=20,000 fire leaves cnt_total = (last retire) + 20,000. Every one of the 21 fits: 20,023 = 23+20k, 20,038 = 38+20k, 20,068, 20,075, 20,897 = 897+20k, 44,969 = 24,969+20k. All 21 are WATCHDOG_MAX, not TIMEOUT_MAX.
verdicts.what_is_true: Every one of the 21 in-simulation non-settling runs ended with at least one PE in P_ERROR raised by the fabric's own watchdog, at a point far inside the simulation budget. This is Property 2 outcome (c), observed 21 times, on real compiler output, with zero accompanying wrong roots (SIM_FAIL_BYPASS = 0 everywhere). The remaining non-settling cases -- 1 wall-clock kill on max_mod_fat among the 39, and 5 on maxp_mod_fat -- are genuinely undiagnosable, because the simulator was killed externally and no perf vector was printed.
verdicts.consequence: ADD ANALYSIS on data in hand -- the highest-value item in T01 and the reason no new experiment is needed. Three sentences in Sec 7.2 plus the derivation in the companion: '22 of the 2,844 attempted configurations did not settle. For 21 of them the retained per-PE cycle counters stop between 20,023 and 44,975 cycles against a testbench budget of 204,700 to 1,638,300, and each equals a last-retirement cycle plus exactly WATCHDOG_MAX = 20,000: these are fabric watchdog fail-stops, Property 2 outcome (c), and they are the campaign's only direct observation of it. The remaining one exceeded the simulator wall-clock cap. No configuration in the campaign produced a finite root differing from the canonical one.' This costs about 0.15 page, converts four reviewers' 'silently excluded' objection into a result, and requires no simulation. Reject the alternatives: re-running with transcript capture (r12, r09) costs ~120 core-hours to learn what the counters already prove; staying silent loses the round because four independent reviewers found the omission unprompted.

verdicts.finding: Eight of the forty instances elaborate more PEs than the G reported in the suite and invariance tables.
verdicts.observed: Ran sprs_core.build_topology(topology, G) for all 40 rows of benchmarks/instances.csv and compared topo.n_nodes to the declared n_gpus: npow2g_small_mesh 5->6 (mesh_3x2), npow2_tiny_hc 7->8 (hypercube_3d), npow2_small_torus 10->12 (torus_4x3), med_dense_mesh 8->9 (mesh_3x3), med_full_torus 128->132 (torus_12x11), large_unbal_torus 32->36 (torus_6x6), vlarge2_dense_2d 128->132 (torus_12x11), maxp_bal_2d 2048->2070 (torus_46x45). The RTL CSV corroborates: the maxp_bal_2d failure row's Error string is '[FAIL] 8192L 2070G torus_46x45: TIMEOUT' and its PerfAllGPUs vector has 2,070 entries.
verdicts.what_is_true: Mesh, torus and hypercube constructors round the worker count up to a rectangle or a power of two, so the elaborated fabric is larger than the tabulated G on 8 of 40 instances. The paper's headline reshape example ('$G{=}128$ on a torus at $N{=}128$', main.tex:2165-2167) is in fact a 132-PE torus.
verdicts.consequence: EDIT, one footnote, essentially zero page cost. 'For mesh, torus and hypercube, $G$ is rounded up to the nearest realisable fabric ($6, 8, 12, 9, 132, 36, 132, 2070$ PEs on the eight affected instances); the tabulated $G$ is the requested worker count.' It costs nothing and it is the kind of small precision that signals care. Low priority relative to X1, X2, X5.

verdicts.finding: Claim 1's stated observable is the root DMEM value, which is never read.
verdicts.observed: Settled in theme T07 as D144 (CONFIRMED): the testbench compares u_sys.gen_node[root_gpu].u_cn.result (src/sprs_core.py:5573) and 'result' is the ALU latch written at rtl/btree_fsm_fast.sv:804-806 and :831-833, never DMEM. I re-read the emitter to confirm the comparison line and the absence of any DMEM read in the testbench: the only other DMEM traffic in the TB is load_gci. Not re-derived beyond that.
verdicts.what_is_true: Claim 1's quantified observable (the root DMEM slot) and the measured observable (the root PE's final COMPUTE result) are different quantities.
verdicts.consequence: EDIT Claim 1's observable, per T07-D144. It belongs in T01's ledger too because it is part of the narrowest-supported-claim rewrite: the restated Claim 1 must name the ALU result, not DMEM, or the narrowing is incomplete.

verdicts.finding: The reproducibility checklist's SHA-256 of the make_leaf_val source is not reproducible from the artifact.
verdicts.observed: main.tex:3094-3098 states 'SHA-256 of the \sv{make\_leaf\_val} source: 20aae138844da00e165cd0a490f7960d3dd806f11ed51950bc3be40600800bb1'. make_leaf_val is a nested function inside emit_sv_testbench (src/sprs_core.py:5364-5378), so inspect.getsource on the module attribute fails. I extracted the exact source span and hashed it under eight conventions -- raw slice, strip, rstrip, textwrap.dedent, dedent+strip, with and without a trailing newline, and the whole file -- and none matches (raw 40dfa098..., strip fe84c9df..., dedent 8e2ee920..., whole file 530a4716...).
verdicts.what_is_true: The digest may well be correct under some convention the paper does not state. As released, no reader can reproduce it, because neither the byte range nor the normalisation is specified and the paper does not ship the command that produced it.
verdicts.consequence: EDIT: either delete the digest or replace it with a reproducible one-liner ('sha256sum of lines 5364-5378 of src/sprs_core.py'). A hash a reader cannot check is worse than no hash in a reproducibility appendix -- it is the one place a referee will actually try to run something. Zero page cost either way.

verdicts.finding: Is the result significant enough to survive the narrowing? (theme framing)
verdicts.observed: Not a factual question. The factual inputs are settled: the measurement is real (T07-X1), the denominator is 2,844/2,822/22, the refinement axis is unevidenced, and the campaign is exhaustive over the (S2,S3) grid rather than top-15.
verdicts.what_is_true: What the evidence supports and what the paper claims differ on four quantifiers (refinements, the DMEM observable, the leaf vector, and the topology family $\T$). Whether the narrowed claim still carries a Q1 contribution is a judgement for the debate.
verdicts.consequence: Hand to the debate. My input: the narrowed claim is stronger-sounding than the current one once X2 and X5 are folded in, because 'complete grid, no selection, and the only failures are fabric fail-stops we can identify' reads as rigour, whereas '2,822 configurations, zero divergence' reads as a number without a denominator.

headline: The denominator is 2,844 attempted / 2,822 passing / 22 non-settling, not 32 -- the 32 that four reviewers report is a row count in live_hw_results_p1_maxpe.csv inflated by ten retries of two configurations, and the file the table generator actually reads (live_hw_results_p1_unified.csv) has exactly 2,844 rows and 22 failures. None of 2,844, 2,854, 2,920, 22 or 32 appears anywhere in main.tex or the companion, and 122.9 of the campaign's 1,003.3 core-hours are spent on runs the paper never mentions. The two most consequential things I found are not in the docket. First, the 21 in-simulation failures are provably fabric watchdog fail-stops, derivable with no re-simulation: cnt_total freezes on leaving P_RUN/P_DRAIN (btree_fsm_fast.sv:885-902), the retained PerfAllGPUs vectors stop 5x-82x below the testbench loop cap, all_done = &cn_done was low, and every stopping cycle equals a last retirement plus exactly WATCHDOG_MAX = 20,000 -- so these 21 runs are the paper's only direct observation of Property 2 outcome (c) and it is currently thrown away. Second, the paper UNDERSTATES its own coverage twice: Sec 7.1 says the top 15 configurations per instance were promoted to xsim, but sprs_tournament.py:1204-1240 queues every deduplicated testbench and select_winners(max_per=15) runs only afterwards -- the campaign is the complete 18x10 (S2,S3) grid on all 40 instances, deduplicated, with no makespan selection touching the invariance evidence at all (Table X's own TBs column, up to 141, contradicts the prose). Against that, one quantifier in Claim 1 has zero evidence of any kind: the s4 field is 'none' in 7,200 of 7,200 compiled and 2,822 of 2,822 validated configurations, so 'all valid ... refinements $r$' and the '$(\asgn,\map,r)$ triple' language at main.tex:2170 must go, and the Phase-2 bullet at main.tex:2066 describes work with no released output. r03's and r07's count of eight single-(G,topology) rows is exact, but seven of those eight do vary the worker count actually populated (only N=200 is a true singleton), and 116 configurations the compiler rejected for IMEM overflow were simulated anyway with enlarged IMEM and 113 sit inside the headline 2,822. Of the 13 docket issues, 9 are CONFIRMED and 4 CONFIRMED_NARROWER (D039, D048, D066, D077); across the 22 verdicts recorded here 16 are CONFIRMED, 4 CONFIRMED_NARROWER, 1 UNVERIFIABLE and 1 INTERPRETIVE; nothing is refuted, though two supporting sub-numbers are wrong (r05's '16 of 32 with positive cycles' is 21, and r09's 20,897 cluster is the 20,000-cycle watchdog, not the 10,000-cycle stall timer, which also voids the '96% of the liveness ceiling' scalability worry). No new experiment is warranted anywhere in T01; the entire theme is served by claim narrowing, one disclosure paragraph, one analysis of retained counters, and a 15-line fix to tools/smoke_test.sh whose step 4 I executed and showed cannot fail even under a deliberately scrambled assignment.

true_denominator.breakdown: Unique ABI-compliant program images emitted across the 40-instance suite: 2,920 (from 7,200 compilations = 40 instances x the complete 18x10 (S2,S3) grid, deduplicated by testbench SHA-256). Of these, 2,844 belong to the 39 HW-validated instances and 76 to maxp_mod_fat. On the 39: 2,844 attempted, 2,822 passed, 22 did not settle -- 21 fabric WATCHDOG_MAX fail-stops (vlarge2_mod_ring 10 ring, vlarge_dense_hc 7 hypercube, max_bal_2d 1 and maxp_bal_2d 1 torus, max_dense_hc 1 and maxp_dense_hc 1 hypercube; zero on linear, mesh or fat-tree) and 1 simulator wall-clock kill (max_mod_fat, fat-tree). On maxp_mod_fat: 5 attempted, all wall-clock kills, 71 never attempted. Retries inflate the row count in live_hw_results_p1_maxpe.csv to 2,854 rows / 32 non-passing (max_mod_fat/tb_2f_3a_none x10, maxp_bal_2d/tb_2f_3a_none x2); the correct configuration-level figures are 2,844 and 22. Zero SIM_FAIL_BYPASS rows and zero root mismatches anywhere. Cost: 821.5 core-h on passing runs (= the reported \WallTotalH), 122.9 core-h on the 32 non-settling rows (undisclosed), 58.9 core-h on maxp_mod_fat (disclosed in L0); campaign total 1,003.3 core-h. Composition caveat: 116 of the 2,844 were flagged E_IMEM_OF by the compiler's own S5 pass (max_imem 518-1792 vs the 512 budget) and were simulated with IMEM widened to the next power of two; 113 of those are inside the 2,822.

narrowest_supported_claim: Across the 2,844 distinct ABI-compliant program images obtained by compiling the complete 18x10 assignment-by-mapping grid on 39 hardware-validated instances -- sixteen leaf counts $N \in [8,8192]$, requested worker counts $G \in [2,4096]$ (elaborated fabrics of 2 to 2,070 PEs) and six direct-network topologies -- 2,822 simulations terminated, and in every one of them the root PE's final COMPUTE result was bit-identical to the canonical root $\Rcan(N,L)$ predicted by the software oracle for that $N$; the remaining 22 did not terminate (21 fabric watchdog fail-stops, one simulator wall-clock kill) and no configuration in the campaign produced a finite root differing from $\Rcan(N,L)$. The campaign evaluates one leaf vector per $N$ and the identity refinement throughout; eight of the sixteen leaf counts are represented by a single requested $(G,\text{topology})$ point, and 2,403 of the 2,822 configurations lie at leaf counts with two or more.
